title: ConfigMaps hold ordinary settings
summary: A ConfigMap stores non-secret configuration. An application may read selected values through environment variables or files.
introduction: A ConfigMap stores non-secret configuration. An application may read selected values through environment variables or files. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A ConfigMap stores non-secret configuration. An application may read selected values through environment variables or files.

blocks.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: club-settings
data:
  WELCOME_TEXT: "Hello, club"
blocks.title: ConfigMaps hold ordinary settings

blocks.text: The ConfigMap contains an ordinary welcome message. It is not a secure place for passwords.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Use the appropriate secret-management approach for real credentials; a ConfigMap is not one.
For more detail later, use this [Kubernetes further reading](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tutorials/kubernetes-basics/).

seo.title: Kubernetes: ConfigMaps hold ordinary settings
